fields.v: No SDD approach. CoReMem (Coding-Repository Memory): (M1) prospective segment valuation yielding a memory template built on 'anchors' (repository locations and executable checks); (M2) cost-internalizing on-policy post-training (reward charges steps inside success); (M3) provenance-gated value credit. 'CoReMem w/o training' = memory on frozen actor. Version: N/A

Memory.md written by the actor at the end of each task, before the next task is known: task block (STATUS, TESTS with exit codes, VERIFY commands, DID/WHERE/FILES) and repository block (CONTEXT, WHERE: layout and how to test); reasoning text and scratch files dropped. Keeps the median step saving of the full trajectory with 6% of its bytes

Harness: mini-swe-agent (98K window) for all; success criterion: overall resolve rate on ChainSWE test boundaries; format Res% / steps / total K tokens. Qwen3.5-9B: no memory 14.0/98.2/98.3; full history 14.2/72.8/85.9; Mem0 16.4/93.8/111.4; MemOp 15.0/94.9/131.7; ReasoningBank 14.6/94.3/166.1; CoReMem w/o training 15.5/95.1/111.7; CoReMem (post-trained) 17.7/72.4/79.9 (works: quality and cost). Qwen3.8-27B-FP8: no memory 21.0/35.1/32.2; full history 22.4/32.6/39.0; Mem0 21.5/35.9/68.7; MemOp 23.4/33.5/50.4; ReasoningBank 25.2/34.3/67.5; CoReMem w/o training 23.4/31.8/32.4; CoReMem 25.7/29.2/28.5 (works). Gemma-4-31B: no memory 11.5/29.9/32.4; full history 11.8/27.2/31.8; Mem0 10.8/28.1/47.2; MemOp 12.8/28.8/49.6; ReasoningBank 13.2/30.4/65.3; CoReMem w/o training 12.5/28.3/33.9; CoReMem 14.2/28.5/29.3 (works). API models, frozen (Table 3): Claude Opus 5.5 no memory 38.5% / 12.6 steps / 21.5K, CoReMem w/o training 38.5% / 11.8 steps / 20.1K (quality unchanged, cost partly); GPT-5.6 Luna no memory 23.6% / 17.9 / 51.7K, CoReMem w/o training 25.7% / 16.3 / 52.5K (-9% steps); DeepSeek-V4-Flash 21.9% / 90.0 / 84.4K vs 23.6% / 78.2 / 82.3K (-13% steps). Existing memory layers (Mem0, MemOp, ReasoningBank): quality partly, cost does not work (more total tokens than no memory on all six models, +13% to +127%; more than CoReMem w/o training on five of six). Ablations (27B, ablation): resolve-only RL 30.4 steps; M1+M2 29.7 steps; full 29.2; misplaced memory cost +2.1 steps without value credit vs +0.3 with it
fields.why: Existing memory layers spend more total tokens than no memory on all six models (Tables 1 and 3); 'five of six' in the paper is against CoReMem w/o training, not against no memory. API token values added from Table 3 (table reads cleanly, not jumbled)

fields.v: Tasks: ChainSWE test half (48 chains, 96 boundaries), disjoint repositories from training. Configurations: 7 memory conditions x 3 open-weight actors (post-trained) + 6 conditions x 3 API actors (frozen). Baseline: no memory on same actor. Held constant: harness (mini-swe-agent), window, step limits per model, memory-layer official instructions. Repetitions: replays 12 (9B frozen), 6-7 (27B), 6 (DeepSeek), 3 (Gemma, Luna), 1 (Opus). Checkpoint rule fixed in advance. Human intervention: none

CoReMem w/o training lowers steps on all six actors (significantly on three, by 9-13%) without lowering resolution, total tokens within -7% to +5% of no memory on five of six; Mem0/MemOp/ReasoningBank cost more tokens than CoReMem on five of six. Post-trained CoReMem: steps -17% to -26%, total tokens -9% to -19%, resolution +22% to +27% relative, resolve per total token +38% to +46% (avg 41%). 27B frozen memory: resolve 21.3% -> 23.4% (+2.1 [+0.4, +3.7]). Significance via paired chain-cluster bootstrap

Distinguished memory layers on effort (steps, tokens); resolution differences small, intervals sometimes include zero; replays vary by model (1 for Opus). Generalisation checks on SWE-bench Verified, two external chain benchmarks and OpenHands harness

Main experiments on Python repositories and mini-swe-agent harness; post-training on three open-weight actors only; other languages and larger actors untested; no wall-clock latency or energy; how memory should be accumulated and refreshed over long repository histories is future work. Ethics: memory may retain paths, commands, test output; should follow access control, redact secrets
